q: The notion of Borel reducibility E ≤_B F (E is Borel reducible to F) means:
opts: E and F have the same number of classes
There is a Borel function f: X → Y such that x E x' ↔ f(x) F f(x')
E ⊆ F as sets of pairs
The Borel complexity of E is less than that of F
exp: E ≤_B F: a Borel reduction is a Borel function f with xEx' ↔ f(x)Ff(x'). This measures relative difficulty of classification: E ≤_B F means classifying E-classes is no harder than classifying F-classes (in a Borel way). The Borel reducibility order is rich and far from linear.
